doc: Named, NON-OVERLAPPING strategic CONTROL REGIONS for dm3 ('The Abandoned Base').
These replace the #315 demo's coarse blanket nearest-landmark snap (a 600 qu radius
over 26 raw landmarks), which produced phantom intra-area 'legs' like RA.low<->RA and
YA.box<->YA. Each region MERGES an item's sub-points / adjacent fixtures into ONE named
area (e.g. RA absorbs RA + RA.low + RA.rox; YA absorbs YA + YA.box + YA.up; SNG absorbs
the SNG nest + SNG.MH + SNG.low + SNG.ledge + SNG.lifts), so those phantom shuffles
collapse into a single region. This is the assignment layer the #319 route segmenter
consumes (a leg = a transition between two DISTINCT region visits).
GEOMETRY MODEL: each region is a SPHERE = center (x,y,z in quake units) + radius_qu.
Assignment (scripts/map_regions.py:assign_region) is DETERMINISTIC NEAREST-REGION-WITH-CAP:
a position is assigned to the region whose 3D-Euclidean center is NEAREST, but only if
that nearest distance is <= that region's radius_qu; otherwise None (a mid-corridor /
transition position is not forced onto a region). Because assignment is nearest-wins,
regions can NEVER double-assign a point (a point belongs to exactly one region or None),
so the radii are membership CAPS, not hard partitions, and may visually overlap without
ambiguity. 3D distance is used deliberately: dm3 is heavily multi-level (water floor
z=-416, hill/bridge z~=-192/-120, RL/window z~=-104/44, Quad/Ring z~=40, RA z~=130-304),
so the Z term cleanly separates stacked areas (e.g. GL/LG water level under the bridge;
Pent pocket under RL) that 2D circles would conflate.
Centers are anchored on each area's PRIMARY strategic item (the named control point in
docs/notes/dm3-route-taxonomy.md), nudged toward the cluster body; radii are tuned to
absorb that area's own sub-points/fixtures while leaving genuine connecting corridors
(RA.tunnel, bridge) as their own small regions. Wide ambient edge-pickups (a far rocket
or shell box at an area boundary) may fall outside all caps and read as None; that is
intended -- they are transition zones, not control points.
GRANULARITY IS A TUNABLE DESIGN CHOICE: which sub-points merge into which named region
(notably YA<->YA.box, which the taxonomy lists as a real ~598 qu MED leg but is merged
here to kill the phantom shuffle; and SNG vs SNG.tele, kept SPLIT because the teleporter
pocket is functionally distinct in openings) is open to reviewer/owner adjustment. Edit
this file (center/radius/membership) without touching the loader or its tests.

regions.name: RA
regions.note: Red Armor — the economy. Merges the RA armor, RA.low (NG) and RA.rox boxes. RA.tunnel (the lower corridor toward Ring) is a SEPARATE region.

regions.name: RA.tunnel
regions.note: Lower tunnel/spawn corridor connecting RA<->Ring. Kept separate so RA<->Ring legs are not swallowed into RA.

regions.name: Ring
regions.note: Ring of Shadows (invis) — busiest central corridor hub; artifact + nails/shells/rockets + t2 teleport destination.

regions.name: mega
regions.note: Central Megahealth on the 'hill', below Quad/Ring. Anchored exactly on the mh entity.

regions.name: RL
regions.note: Rocket Launcher (firepower unit) + co-located nails + spawn. window teleport-dst sits just inside its cap.

regions.name: YA
regions.note: Yellow Armor pocket — MERGED: the YA.box armor + the YA ledge (SSG/rockets) + YA.up. The taxonomy lists YA<->YA.box as a real ~598 qu MED leg; merged here to kill the phantom shuffle (granularity is tunable).

regions.name: Pent
regions.note: Pentagram (invuln) pocket, low in the SE. Anchored on the artifact; the far 'Pent' Megahealth (~850 qu east) is NOT in this region (it falls to None).

regions.name: SNG
regions.note: Super Nailgun nest — MERGED: SNG gun + SNG.MH (mega) + SNG.low + SNG.ledge + SNG.lifts. SNG.tele is a SEPARATE region.

regions.name: SNG.tele
regions.note: SNG teleporter source pocket (NW), functionally distinct from the SNG nest in opening rotations (SNG-tele->Ring->RA).

regions.name: LG
regions.note: Lightning Gun on the east water shelf (z=-416). Absorbs the east water rockets/cells. Separated from GL by the Z floor + distance.

regions.name: GL
regions.note: Grenade Launcher + west/central water floor (z=-416). The far far-west/east ambient water cells at the basin edges may read None.

regions.name: bridge
regions.note: The bridge connector spanning the chasm above the water level, between RL/YA and the basin.
